name: Kudzu root extract (Pueraria lobata)
short: Review caution: long-term kudzu root use during heavy drinking may raise acetaldehyde-related cancer risk. Placebo trials in heavy drinkers: adverse events like placebo; none serious from kudzu.
text: In double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of kudzu extract in adults who drink heavily or have alcohol use disorder: in 120 adults with alcohol use disorder who binge drink, randomized to kudzu extract by mouth taken as needed (on days when binge drinking was anticipated) or placebo, with weekly counselling, for 12 weeks, the overall frequency of adverse events was similar in both groups, with no serious adverse events related to kudzu; a randomized 4-week trial in 17 young men found no adverse events and no changes in vital signs, blood chemistry or kidney or liver function, and its conclusion describes minimal side effects; and an 8-week study in 19 men and women with alcohol use disorder (9 in the kudzu group) noted no adverse events or safety concerns. In an open-label 4-week study, 50 postmenopausal women taking kudzu root extract at five different dose schedules found it well tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported. Interaction with alcohol: in a crossover study in 12 healthy adults who drank moderately, 9 days of kudzu extract did not change how intoxicated they felt or their balance and reaction time after alcohol, but blood alcohol rose slightly faster for 10 to 15 minutes after the higher alcohol dose, with no difference in peak level, and kudzu enhanced that dose's effects on heart rate and skin temperature. A 2007 review notes that kudzu root (unlike the flower, Pueraria flos) inhibits the enzyme ALDH2 and increases acetaldehyde, and cautions, in an abstract that reports no human outcome data, that chronic use at times of high alcohol intake, as in hangover products, may predispose people to acetaldehyde-related tumours; it suggests recommendations similar to those for disulfiram, a medicine that also inhibits ALDH2. No other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
